A single dose of intravenous dexamethasone at 1 mg/kg, capped at 10 mg, did not significantly attenuate the IL-6 response after paediatric cardiopulmonary bypass. The higher heart rate and longer intensive care stay observed in the dexamethasone group should be treated as exploratory because allocation was nonrandom and perioperative complexity was not adjusted for.

title: Hormonal contraceptive users exhibit increased approach responses to higher reward in an online approach-avoidance task.
abstract: Hormonal contraceptives (HOC) are used worldwide; however, there are controversies regarding their effects on mental health with studies reporting HOC to be associated with mood symptoms, especially depression and anxiety. Costly avoidance, i.e., avoiding a potentially rewarding situation to minimize anticipated emotional distress, is thought to be a key component of affective disorders. This study aims to explore the relationship between the use of hormonal contraceptives, symptoms of depression and anxiety, and costly avoidance. Self-reported users of HOC (n = 139) and non-users (n = 209) completed the Inventory of Depression and Anxiety Symptoms (IDAS-II) and partook in an online approach-avoidance conflict task assessing costly avoidance. Statistical analyses included generalized mixed effects models, t-tests and Mann-Whitney U tests. HOC users showed increased odds of approach behavior in the highest reward level. No direct associations were found between approach behavior and depression and anxiety symptoms. Upon further post-hoc analysis, HOC use did not moderate any association between approach behavior and affective symptoms. In line with previous literature, HOC users showed less avoidant behavior than non-users. Results should be interpreted with caution, as the observational nature of the study opens up to self-selection bias. However, this represents an important first observation that warrants further longitudinal and/or placebo-controlled studies.

title: Performance of the NightWatch seizure detection device on the leg compared to the standard arm placement: A pilot study.
abstract: Nighttime monitoring is crucial for individuals with epilepsy, both to reduce the risk of injuries and to help prevent sudden unexpected death in epilepsy. NightWatch, a seizure detection device that can detect nocturnal seizures by using heart rate (HR) and movement parameters, has been shown to be effective when worn on the upper arm. This study piloted whether wearing NightWatch on the lower leg provides comparable seizure detection sensitivity. In this prospective pilot study, NightWatch users wore a second device on the lower leg for four weeks. The positive percent agreement (PPA) was determined for the leg-worn NightWatch compared to the arm module. Differences in signal quality and time spent in rest state (sensor in horizontal position) were evaluated both per participant and across the population. Ten participants (mean age: 12.5 years, range = 5-25) were included in the study. In total, 245 nights were analyzed. PPA ranged from 11.1% to 100%, yielding an overall mean PPA of 76.8% and median of 100%. The quality of HR signal for the leg module was comparable to the arm module (p = 0.1602). The leg module showed variability across patients and, overall, registered the rest state significantly less often than the arm module (p = 0.0059). This pilot study demonstrated that NightWatch performance on the leg varies across participants, with comparable results to arm use in some participants but reduced accuracy in others. This study has been registered in the Overview of Medical Research in the Netherlands (OMON) (NL-OMON57506).

title: Serum context shapes macrophage baseline state and LPS responsiveness in human monocyte-derived macrophages.
abstract: Human monocyte-derived macrophages (MDMs) are central to translational immunology, yet most differentiation protocols rely on xenogeneic fetal calf serum (FCS), which may alter macrophage functional states. Autologous serum (AS) maintains the donor-specific immunometabolic milieu, but its impact on macrophage baseline programming and stimulus responsiveness has not been systematically evaluated. Monocytes from 32 healthy donors were differentiated in parallel with 10% AS or FCS for five days with M-CSF, followed by 24-hour stimulation with LPS, IL-4/IL-10/TGF-β, or vehicle. Cytokine secretion was quantified by multiplex assay, activation markers by qPCR, and baseline transcriptional programs by bulk RNA sequencing. AS- versus FCS-differentiated MDMs showed significantly greater LPS-induced secretion of TNF-α, IL-6, IL-1β, IP-10, IL-23, TARC and IL-1RA together with higher CD86 and CCR7 expression, whereas these differences were not observed following IL-4/IL-10/TGF-β stimulation or in unstimulated cells. Transcriptomic analysis of unstimulated MDMs identified distinct serum-dependent baseline programs, with FCS associated with increased expression of inflammatory cytokines, chemokines, and innate immune activation genes, whereas AS was associated with genes involved in lipid metabolism, extracellular matrix remodeling, and immune surveillance. Serum context is a major determinant of macrophage baseline state and inflammatory responsiveness. FCS is associated with a more inflammatory baseline and attenuated LPS-induced activation, while AS shows a metabolically and immunologically homeostatic baseline with greater LPS responsiveness. These findings demonstrate that serum composition shapes basal macrophage programs and differentially modulates responses to inflammatory versus alternative stimulation, supporting consideration of autologous serum when modeling donor-specific innate immune responses.

title: Imagery Reprocessing in the Treatment of PTSD and Psychosis: A Case Illustration.
abstract: Traumatic experiences are strikingly elevated among people with psychosis, yet the post-traumatic stress symptoms they experience have historically been overlooked and undertreated. Concerns that addressing trauma may exacerbate psychotic symptoms have contributed to clinical hesitancy. Encouragingly, a growing body of evidence supports the safety and efficacy of trauma-focused interventions for people experiencing both post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and psychosis. This article demonstrates how imagery-based reprocessing techniques can be used to treat overlapping PTSD and psychosis symptoms. This article presents Hamid, a 22-year-old Kurdish refugee experiencing PTSD and psychosis symptoms, including flashbacks, nightmares, distressing voices, visions, and somatic intrusions, alongside pervasive fears of harm. Hamid was deeply distressed by these experiences, leading to social withdrawal and a diminished quality of life. Hamid attended 26 weekly sessions and 3 booster sessions of Trauma-Focused Cognitive Behavioural Therapy for psychosis (TF-CBTp), an integrative approach combining principles and techniques drawn from cognitive models of PTSD and psychosis. Early sessions focused on collaborative formulation, psychoeducation, and developing strategies to promote a sense of control through emotional regulation, to support readiness for trauma-focused work. The central phase employed imagery-based memory reprocessing techniques to address unhelpful meanings (cognitive appraisals), update traumatic memories, meet emotional needs, and reduce the emotional intensity of both PTSD- and psychosis-related symptoms. By the end of therapy, Hamid reported fewer trauma-related intrusions, reduced distress linked to his voices and somatic experiences, and a growing sense of safety in his daily life enabling him to begin re-engaging socially. A comprehensive Staying Well Plan was developed to maintain this progress and continue rebuilding his life.

title: The Stanford Multifaceted Dissociation Questionnaire: A 9-Item Measure of Trait and State Dissociation.
abstract: Dissociation is a common and increasingly studied phenomenon with substantial relevance for mental health. To date, researchers have often relied upon broad conceptualizations and retrospective measures, making it difficult to identify a consistent subset of experiences for dissociation, explore their links to related phenomena, and differentiate habitual from momentary dissociation. To address these issues, we introduce the Stanford Multifaceted Dissociation Questionnaire (SMDQ), a 9-item measure that assesses three facets of dissociation and can be employed to assess either trait or state dissociation. In Study 1, we evaluated the content validity of the initial SMDQ item pool using feedback from individuals with lived experience of dissociation (N = 73) and content experts (N = 14), detailing our focus on detachment-type experiences that may help the dissociation construct to be more cleanly distinguished from other clinical phenomena. In Study 2 (N = 400), we described the item selection process and examined the factor structure, internal consistency, and convergent/discriminant validity of both the trait and state versions of the SMDQ. In Study 3 (N = 500), we further investigated the psychometric properties of both versions, including their factor structure, measurement invariance, internal consistency, test-retest reliability, and convergent/discriminant validity. Across the studies, scores on the trait and state versions of the SMDQ showed strong content validity and a theoretically congruent factor structure, comprised of alteration in the perception of one's mind, body, and world (suggesting a tripartite model of dissociation). This structure was largely invariant across demographic groups and time. We also demonstrate good convergent and discriminant validity, internal consistency (ω > 0.80), and temporal stability over 1 week (r > 0.70 for the trait version). Overall, we conclude that the trait and state versions of the SMDQ are promising measurement tools that can enhance our understanding of dissociation's structure, antecedents, and consequences.

title: TFEB overexpression in excitatory neurons ameliorates amyloid-β pathology via coordinated enhancement of autophagy-lysosome and mitochondrial function.
abstract: The intraneuronal accumulation of amyloid-β (Aβ) is an early pathogenic event in Alzheimer's disease (AD), initiating a pathological cascade that includes synaptic dysfunction, metabolic deficits, and eventual neuronal loss. Transcription factor EB (TFEB), a master regulator of the autophagy-lysosomal pathway (ALP) and mitochondrial homeostasis, represents a promising therapeutic target. However, its efficacy and mechanisms when specifically activated in neurons during the prodromal stage remain unclear. Here, we used an adeno-associated virus (AAV) under the control of the CaMKIIα promoter to achieve excitatory neuron-specific TFEB overexpression in the hippocampal CA1 region of 2 months-old 5×FAD mice. This intervention significantly reduced soluble Aβ levels at 3 months and attenuated amyloid plaque burden, dystrophic neurite formation, and glial activation at 6 months, accompanied by substantial improvements in spatial learning and memory. Mechanistically, transcriptomic and functional analyses revealed that TFEB not only enhanced autophagic flux and lysosomal biogenesis but also promoted the expression of key mitochondrial genes and improved mitochondrial function. In APP695swe-N2a cells, TFEB overexpression increased levels of LC3B-II and LAMP1, enhanced mitochondrial activity and biogenesis (via PGC-1α upregulation), and effectively reduced intracellular Aβ accumulation. Our findings demonstrate that targeted TFEB overexpression in excitatory neurons during early AD pathogenesis initiates a protective cascade by co-activating autophagy-lysosomal clearance and mitochondrial pathways, thereby reducing Aβ accumulation and mitigating downstream pathology. This study highlights the potential of neuron-specific TFEB activation as a cell-type-specific therapeutic approach for early AD intervention. © 2026 The Pathological Society of Great Britain and Ireland.

title: Valence- and locus-specific attributional patterns across manic, depressive, and euthymic presentations of bipolar disorder: A cross-sectional study.
abstract: Attributional biases are relevant to social cognition in bipolar disorder (BD), but whether they vary across clinical presentations remains unclear. We examined attributional patterns during mania, depression, and euthymia relative to healthy controls (HCs). In a two-site, cross-sectional study, 75 adults with DSM-5-defined BD-I/II were assessed during mania (n = 32), depression (n = 21), or euthymia (n = 22), alongside 22 HCs. Participants completed the Internal, Personal and Situational Attributions Questionnaire-Revised (IPSAQ-R), which assesses internal, personal, and situational attributions to positive and negative scenarios. Dominant causes were coded into counts by valence and causal locus and analyzed using adjusted negative binomial generalized estimating equations. The Group × Valence × Locus interaction was significant (Wald χ2(6) = 13.16, P = 0.041). Differences primarily involved negative events. Compared with HCs, mania was associated with fewer situational attributions (incidence rate ratios [IRR] = 0.39, 95% CI [0.23, 0.69]) and higher personal attributions (IRR = 1.34, 95% CI [1.05, 1.72]). Depression was also associated with fewer situational attributions (IRR = 0.60, 95% CI [0.36, 0.99]), without increased personal attributions. After Holm adjustment, only the reduced situational attribution in mania remained significant (pHolm = 0.009). Euthymia did not differ significantly from HCs. Attributional patterns in BD differed across clinical presentations, with differences most evident in mania and depression and less evident in euthymia. Reduced situational attribution in mania was the most robust finding; findings in depression and higher personal attribution in mania were preliminary. These cross-sectional findings are consistent with possible presentation-related variation; longitudinal studies are needed to determine whether attributional patterns change within individuals over time.

title: Academic skills in students with Duchenne muscular dystrophy: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
journal: Child neuropsychology : a journal on normal and abnormal development in childhood and adolescence
abstract: Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD) is a genetic neuromuscular disorder increasingly recognized for its neurocognitive phenotype, including cognitive deficits, behavioral disorders, and learning disabilities. Specific distal dystrophin isoforms (e.g., Dp140 and Dp71) play a critical role in central nervous system function, driving individual variability in cognitive impairment. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to define the academic learning profile of reading, spelling, and math skills in children and adolescents with DMD. We systematically searched five databases up to July 8 2025. We included original, peer-reviewed studies that assessed academic performance (reading, spelling, or math) through standardized tests in patients with DMD (confirmed by elevated creatine kinase, gene mutation, or muscle biopsy). We excluded single-case, qualitative, non-controlled, or review articles. Seven Level III non-randomized case-control studies met the inclusion criteria (312 participants: 177 DMD, 135 controls). A random-effects meta-analysis revealed that students with DMD scored significantly lower than controls in reading and math. Math deficits were more pronounced, constrained by domain-general verbal memory bottlenecks. Quantitative data on spelling were limited, though narrative findings showed parallel vulnerabilities. Subgroup analyses with a small number of comparisons (k = 2) were severely underpowered and treated purely as exploratory. Students with DMD face substantial challenges in acquiring core academic skills. Future studies should consider genotypic profiles and distal isoform variations to help explain individual variability and guide personalized educational support. Future longitudinal research with well-matched control cohorts is needed to clarify long-term cognitive and academic trajectories.

title: Understanding the conceptual layers of 'sympathetic': Implications for autonomic neuroscience.
Facial Nerve Preservation Versus Sacrifice in Parotid Malignancies With Tumor-Nerve Adhesion: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: To compare oncologic outcomes and facial motor function between nerve-preserving (NP) dissection and nerve-sacrificing (NS) resection with immediate reconstruction in malignant parotid tumors where the facial nerve is closely associated, degenerated, but anatomically identifiable. The authors retrospectively reviewed patients with malignant parotid tumors treated at a single tertiary center from February 2020 to February 2022. Cases with intraoperative tumor-nerve adhesion and neural degeneration were assigned to either the NP or NS group. Propensity score matching was applied to reduce confounding. Outcomes included recurrence-free survival, event-free survival, and facial nerve function at last follow-up. One hundred forty-five patients were included (96 NPs, 49 NS). After matching, each group included 47 patients. Recurrence-free survival was 74.5% versus 76.6% and event-free survival was 68.1% versus 59.6% in the NP dissection and nerve resection with reconstruction groups, respectively (P>0.05). Cox multivariate regression analysis showed that neither nerve management nor radiotherapy influenced recurrence-free or event-free survival (P>0.05). Facial nerve function at final follow-up was significantly associated with intraoperative management (P<0.001). Binary logistic regression analysis confirmed that nerve resection significantly increased the risk of postoperative facial paralysis (odds ratio=11.358, 95% confidence interval: 3.805-33.899, P<0.001). In malignant parotid tumors where the facial nerve is degenerated but anatomically identifiable, nerve sacrifice does not improve oncologic outcomes but leads to significantly worse facial function. Nerve preservation should be performed whenever possible.

title: Transposons contribute to splice-isoform diversity in the Drosophila brain.
abstract: The extraordinary complexity of the brain depends in part on the vast diversity of mRNA isoforms it expresses, often in a cell-type specific manner. In a recent study, we found that intronic transposable elements (TEs) are spliced into neural transcripts and diversify the splice isoform repertoire of neurons and glia (Treiber and Waddell, 2020). A recent paper by Azad et al. revisits these findings using their TIDAL analysis pipeline applied to our published data (Azad et al., 2024). Their analysis did not find any of the splicing reads we reported and although they used RT-PCR to test seven of the 264 TE-gene pairs we had previously reported, they failed to validate TE-gene splicing in any of them. Here, we conduct a quantitative analysis of TE exonisation and show that intronic TE insertions are frequently recruited as alternative exons, with exon usage ranging from rare events to near-complete inclusion in transcripts. We implement this analysis in an improved version of our TEChim software and present clear support for TE-gene splicing at the seven loci tested by Azad et al. We also identify methodological issues in the experimental and computational design of the Azad et al. study that likely explains their failure to detect TE-gene chimeras, while demonstrating that TE-gene splicing can be detected by RT-PCR under appropriate experimental conditions. Together, our data demonstrates that TE splice isoforms are not rare artefacts but measurable and biologically relevant features of the Drosophila brain transcriptome that may contribute to the molecular complexity and functional adaptability of the brain.

title: Long-Range Temporal Correlations in Brain-State Dynamics via a Multivariate One-Hot Approach.
abstract: Temporal sequences of discrete brain states provide a symbolic representation of large-scale neural dynamics. Here, we introduce a one-hot detrended fluctuation analysis (DFA) formulation to quantify long-range temporal correlations in the recurrence dynamics of individual states, independent of the embedding geometry or the symbolic transition encoding. Applied to resting-state Electroencephalographic microstate sequences acquired under eyes-open (EO) and eyes-closed (EC) conditions, the method reveals heterogeneous scaling exponents across states and a global increase in scaling under EC, indicating condition-dependent modulation of multi-timescale organization. Systematic surrogate manipulations disentangle the structural sources of scaling. Disrupting state lifetime statistics through microstate duration equalization or randomization markedly reduces the Hurst exponent, whereas transition-order shuffling alone produces comparatively minor changes in absolute scaling. These findings indicate that long-range dependence is primarily associated with structured state lifetimes rather than with higher-order symbolic syntax. At the same time, transition ordering modulates EO-EC differences, suggesting that symbolic organization contributes to the context-dependent expression of temporal memory. Combined surrogate operations reveal additive effects. The proposed one-hot formulation provides a minimal, representation-invariant characterization of temporal correlations in symbolic sequences and can be generalized to discrete brain-state dynamics obtained from different neuroimaging modalities.

title: Rotary First: A Technique for Simultaneous Root Canal Negotiation and Glide Path Establishment-An In Vitro Study.
abstract: This preliminary in vitro study compared active instrumentation time and instrument fracture between the rotary first technique, which combines engine-driven canal negotiation and glide path establishment, and conventional manual instrumentation. Thirty freshly extracted human maxillary molars (103 canals) with canal curvatures ≤ 30° were randomised at tooth level to the rotary first or manual group. Active instrumentation time was compared separately in palatal (P), distobuccal (DB), mesiobuccal (MB) and second mesiobuccal (MB2) canals using 2-sided Mann-Whitney U-tests with Holm-Bonferroni adjustment. Overall canal-level fracture frequencies were compared exploratorily using a 2-sided Fisher's exact test. Median active instrumentation time was lower with rotary first in every canal type. After multiplicity adjustment, the difference remained statistically significant only in MB canals (6.3 vs. 55.0 s; adjusted P = .004; rrb = 0.70). Differences in P (adjusted P = .087), DB (adjusted P = .100) and MB2 canals (adjusted P = .354) were not statistically significant. Fractures occurred in 7/53 rotary first canals (13.2%) and 2/50 manual canals (4.0%); the difference was not statistically significant (P = .162). Under the restricted anatomical conditions evaluated, rotary first reduced active instrumentation time significantly only in MB canals after adjustment. The fracture comparison was underpowered and did not account for within-tooth clustering; therefore, neither equivalent procedural safety nor the overall superiority of either protocol can be inferred.

title: Genetic Loci Influencing Sex-Specific Social Reinforcement in Heterogeneous Stock Rats.
abstract: Social motivation and reinforcement drive social interactions and are critical for the development and maintenance of social skills and relationships. These behaviors are influenced by sexually dimorphic factors across many species, including mammals. Sex-specific impairments are reported in psychiatric disorders such as autism spectrum disorder, attention deficit hyperactivity disorder, and depression. Despite this, few studies have directly examined normative sex differences in social motivation or heritable genetic factors contributing to their prevalence. We assessed social reinforcement in a large cohort of outbred heterogeneous stock (HS) rats using an operant three-port task (n = 2560). Rats nose-poked into one port for social stimulus access (familiar same-sex conspecific), with the two additional ports offering access to an empty social-stimulus chamber or nonsocial control. Locomotor response to a novel environment was also measured. Consistent with elevated exploratory activity, female rats made more responses, earned more social reinforcers, and spent more time in the social reinforcement port, and male rats demonstrated a higher relative preference for the social port. The genetic basis of individual and sex-dependent variation in social motivation was evaluated using genome-wide association approaches. These behavioral measures were moderately heritable (h2 = 0.071 to 0.249 ± 0.021 to 0.048), and several sex-specific and shared loci of interest were identified. Integration with brain-specific expression quantitative trait loci and coding variants identified several candidate genes (Socs6, Mecr, Oprd1, Sqstm1) with potential roles in social behavior. Together, these findings highlight consistent sex differences in social motivation and provide an initial genetic framework for understanding variability in social reinforcement.

title: Oxygen-Plasma-Induced Surface Reconstruction of WSe2 Enables Nonvolatile Optoelectronic Synapses for in-Sensor Neuromorphic Vision.
abstract: Developing neuromorphic visual systems that integrate sensing, memory, and information processing is important for reducing data-transfer overhead in edge vision. 2D WSe2 offers strong light-matter interaction, but its intrinsically rapid carrier relaxation generally leads to volatile photoresponses that are unfavorable for nonvolatile synaptic weight storage. Here, we develop a two-terminal WSe2 optoelectronic synapse through carefully controlled oxygen-plasma-induced surface reconstruction. The contact-first, plasma-reconstruction-second strategy employs preformed metal electrodes to physically shield the underlying contact regions while allowing the exposed WSe2 surface to undergo reconstruction. The resulting device exhibits persistent photogating, wavelength-dependent optical potentiation, reversible electrical depression, and a large long-term potentiation/depression (LTP/LTD) conductance dynamic range of 426. A high/low resistance state (HRS/LRS) resistance ratio on the order of 105 is maintained together with stable operation over more than 4000 cycles. An experimentally calibrated hardware-software co-simulation further demonstrates the potential of the measured optoelectronic response for front-end noise suppression, highlighting a simple surface-engineering route toward integrated sensing, nonvolatile weight storage, and neuromorphic preprocessing.

title: 'Can I keep myself safe?' in a system lacking support: A qualitative study on overdose risk perceptions by people who co-use benzodiazepine receptor agonists and opioids.
abstract: Co-use of benzodiazepines and z-drugs [collectively termed benzodiazepine receptor agonists (BZRA)] with opioids is involved in a large proportion of drug-related deaths. Historical and contemporary service provision rarely address the intersection between sociologically inherited disadvantage and current unmet treatment needs in people who use drugs. In this qualitative study, we examined people's understandings of overdose risk and what strategies, if any, they implemented to keep themselves safe when co-using BZRAs and opioids. We interviewed 48 people (37 men and 11 women) in community settings who co-use BZRAs and opioids (currently and up to 6 months before the study) in Bristol, Teesside and Glasgow, United Kingdom. We used a semi-structured topic guide to facilitate in-depth exploration of the ways in which people who co-use managed the risks of an overdose and other drug-related harms. Conceptually, we used the socioecological framework to develop the interview topic guide and frame the analysis and interpretation. All data were transcribed and analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. Intrapersonally, people were aware of the risks associated with co-using ('consumption roulette'), especially with illicitly obtained drugs. They tended to interrogate their ability to reduce the risk of overdosing within their social, physical and environmental context ('can I keep myself safe?'). At the intrapersonal level, for those higher in self-efficacy and agency, there was a sense of 'I can keep myself safe' by implementing tried-and-tested risk minimisation strategies, e.g. consuming drugs in small batches. However, among those lower in self-efficacy and agency, feelings of hope- and helplessness resulted in a belief that 'there is nothing you can do'. These narratives related back to participants' perception that system and service-level support was insufficient or lacking altogether ('they don't care about us'). We developed an explanatory self-regulatory model of co-use of benzodiazepine receptor agonists, opioids and risk. Co-use is driven partly by people's attempts to self-medicate, feel normal and function. Negative experiences (e.g. non-fatal overdose) caused most individuals to reconsider risk taking, with some expressing agency and implementing risk minimisation strategies while others felt disempowered by the wider system and the perceived lack of support and care. This lack of systemic support requires people to balance their needs to function against the risks of co-using by themselves.

title: Probing deubiquitinases: from inhibition to activity.
abstract: Deubiquitinating enzymes (DUBs) are a class of isopeptidases that catalyze the removal of ubiquitin from protein substrates or ubiquitin chains, thereby playing a critical role in maintaining cellular homeostasis. Consequently, dysregulation of DUB activity has been implicated in a wide range of diseases, including cancer and neurodegeneration. To better understand the DUB function, chemical probes, small molecules specifically designed to modulate protein function, have emerged as powerful tools. These probes enable precise manipulation of DUB activity, allowing researchers to directly interrogate their enzymatic activity in complex biological systems. By facilitating mechanistic studies and target validation, chemical probes are instrumental in elucidating DUB biology and hold significant promise for therapeutic development. Here, we discuss the evolution of DUB-targeting chemical probes, from early promiscuous inhibitors to highly selective modulators. Focusing on two extensively studied enzymes, USP7 and UCHL1, we highlight how advances in probe design have aided both mechanistic insight and the development of selective modulators.

title: A Biophysical Perspective on Microwave-Induced Neurobiological Effects.
abstract: Microwave radiation interacts with the nervous system through a cascade of electromagnetic, thermal, and mechanical perturbations that drive a broad range of neurobiological responses. Although exposure guidelines are based on specific absorption rate (SAR), substantive evidence indicates that neurobiological effects arise across frequencies, waveforms, and SAR levels that SAR alone cannot characterize. We distinguish net-thermal, transient-thermal, and non-thermal mechanisms according to whether a response is mediated by the net temperature rise, by the heating rate and temperature gradients, or largerly independent of temperature change. This review traces the physical perturbation cascade from electromagnetic field distribution through thermal dynamics to thermoelastic stress, and reviews five biological endpoints: genotoxicity, molecular dysregulation and signaling, blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability, electrophysiology, and behavioral changes. A consistent finding is that many studies report associations with only SAR and frequency, omitting the intermediate physical quantities that drive the responses, and thus obscuring a mechanistic understanding of the causal chain. Mapping of reported studies into the SAR-frequency space reveals a clustering within the 0.9-3 GHz band and near SAR = 2 W/kg, with biological alterations reported below these limits under both continuous and pulsed exposures. These findings motivate future work that directly quantifies spatiotemporal physical perturbations to close the gap between exposure conditions and neurobiological outcomes.

title: Microparticle-Enabled Local Sustained Delivery of Paroxetine for Osteoarthritis Treatment.
abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a prevalent joint disease characterized by irreversible cartilage degradation, chronic pain, and reduced quality of life. Current treatments, including nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) and corticosteroids, are largely palliative, ineffective for some patients, and associated with adverse effects. We have shown that paroxetine (Px), an FDA-approved antidepressant, has potential as a disease-modifying OA drug by inhibiting the G protein-coupled receptor kinase 2 (GRK2). Elevated GRK2 activity drives inflammation, extracellular matrix degradation and cartilage damage in OA. By inhibiting GRK2, Px suppresses cartilage degeneration, enhances chondrocyte anabolic activity, and reduces inflammation in the OA joint. In this study, we develop a local, slow-release drug delivery system that harnesses the therapeutic benefits of Px for OA treatment via microfluidic-assisted encapsulation in size-controlled poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) microparticles (MP). In vitro studies show that the drug release profile is controlled by tuning the MP fabrication parameters. Efficacy testing shows that Px-eluting PLGA microparticles (MP-Px) decrease fibroblast cell migration and proliferation in vitro. In vivo, the intra-articular implantation of MP-Px in the clinically relevant destabilization of medial meniscus mouse OA model decreases chondrocyte apoptosis and has some anti-inflammatory effects in the acute phase of OA. Safranin O staining indicates mild staining loss in MP-treated groups, warranting further assessment of cartilage-matrix safety with long-term use. Importantly, serum Px levels remain low following MP-Px treatment compared with intraperitoneally administered Px (IP-Px). To the best of our knowledge, this biomaterial provides the first local intra-articular delivery of Px. These short-term findings in mice support further preclinical evaluation of MP-Px, including its effects on the cartilage matrix and long-term efficacy.

title: Toward Creating an Injury Severity Index for Experimental Traumatic Brain Injury: Data-Driven and Knowledge-Driven Approaches.
abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) has the highest incidence of all neurological disorders, and is a major source of death and long-term disability worldwide. Yet the seemingly simple act of assessing TBI severity remains a major, unresolved challenge. Central to this challenge is that TBI encompasses a broad class of heterogeneous injuries superimposed on the intrinsic complexity of the mammalian brain. From a biological perspective, TBI impacts multiple scales of analysis from molecular and cellular pathways to neural networks, and from behavior to functional outcomes. These domains span temporal scales that vary from milliseconds to years. Acute assessment of clinical TBI is shifting from reliance on crude categorization of "mild," "moderate," and "severe" TBI to a more nuanced multimodal classification that integrates Clinical assessments, Biomarkers, Imaging, and injury Modifiers (CBI-M) into a single framework. It is critical that the pre-clinical field adopts a similar approach for experimental TBI in order to improve pre-clinical fidelity and translational potential. In pre-clinical TBI, there are unrealized opportunities to synthesize data from a constellation of early functional scores, biomarkers, imaging, and other features to more accurately determine injury severity. We review historic and ongoing efforts to define injury severity in pre-clinical TBI and discuss the need for a data-driven integrative injury severity index with an eye toward bench-to-bedside translation.

title: Diagnostic performance of blood-based biomarker thresholds and ratios across the cognitive continuum in a diverse South Asian cohort.
journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association
abstract: The rising burden of dementia in the Global South is compounded by a substantial diagnostic gap limiting access to biomarker-based diagnosis. We evaluated the diagnostic performance of non-invasive blood-based biomarkers and their ratios across the cognitive continuum in a South Asian cohort to address a lack of evidence beyond Western populations. This study included participants from a Cognitive Disorders Clinic (n = 315), comprising individuals with mild cognitive impairment (MCI), Alzheimer's disease (AD), frontotemporal dementia (FTD), and cognitively unimpaired (CU) controls. All participants underwent standardized cognitive assessment and structural brain imaging. Serum phosphorylated tau (p-tau217), p-tau181, and neurofilament light (NfL) were quantified using a Simoa HD-X analyzer. Diagnostic performance of biomarkers and their ratios were assessed, and a novel multi-threshold approach was applied to facilitate their clinical interpretation in routine practice. Serum p-tau217 and NfL levels were significantly higher in the cognitively impaired group compared to CU, whereas p-tau181 showed no significant difference. Across the diagnostic groups, p-tau217 was highest in AD (F = 12.61, p < 0.001), and NfL in FTD (F = 20.84, p < 0.001). NfL best discriminated FTD versus CU, whereas p-tau217 showed optimal discrimination for AD (area under the curve [AUC] = 0.85). The NfL/p-tau217 ratio improved discrimination between AD and FTD (AUC = 0.78). The multi-threshold approach demonstrated superior diagnostic performance compared to single cut-off. Serum p-tau217, NfL, and NfL/p-tau217 ratio showed robust diagnostic accuracy in this diverse South Asian cohort. The multi-threshold approach improved the clinical interpretability, supporting the integration of blood-based biomarkers (BBMs) in clinical practice, enabling timely diagnosis and accurate determination of therapeutic eligibility.

title: Visit-to-visit blood pressure variability and cognitive decline in the oldest-old.
journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association
abstract: The oldest-old (≥90 years) have a high burden of cognitive impairment, yet the role of blood pressure (BP) variability remains unclear. We examined whether visit-to-visit resting systolic BP variability (rSBPV) is associated with cognitive decline. We analyzed The 90+ Study participants (n = 647) without dementia at baseline who had ≥3 longitudinal BP and cognitive assessments. rSBPV was defined as the root mean square error from within-participant regression of systolic BP on age and categorized as low, medium, or high. Multi-state models estimated transitions between normal cognition, cognitive impairment, and dementia. Compared with medium rSBPV, high rSBPV was associated with higher hazards of transitioning from normal cognition to cognitive impairment (hazard ratio [HR] 1.36, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.05-1.74), from normal cognition to dementia (HR 2.90, 95% CI 1.26-6.69), and from cognitive impairment to dementia (HR 1.44, 95% CI 1.06-1.96). Higher rSBPV is associated with greater cognitive decline in older adults.

title: Association of life-course production work and Lewy body neuropathology.
journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association
abstract: The occupational exposome-the summation of lifetime workplace exposures-impacts Alzheimer's disease and related dementias (ADRD). Examining the role of high-risk occupational exposures on ADRD pathology, including Lewy bodies, may enable disease mitigation strategies. This retrospective cohort study included brain donors with neuropathological characterization (n = 1079, 47.5% female, mean age at death: 80.9). Donor occupational histories were derived and assigned Standardized Occupation Classification Codes. The association between Lewy body neuropathology and "production occupations" (i.e., assemblers, fabricators, manufacturers, etc.) was modeled via logistic regression adjusting for age, sex, and year of death. Lewy bodies were present in 32% of the total sample. Donors with a history of "production occupations" (12%) had 23% increased adjusted odds of having Lewy bodies (adjusted odds ratio = 1.23, 95% confidence interval = 1.11-1.35). This is the first study demonstrating increased levels of Lewy body neuropathology in those with "production occupations." Precise categorization of hazardous exposures is needed to identify mechanistic pathways.

title: A systematic review and meta-analysis on neuropsychological measures in tauopathies.
journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association
abstract: Cognitive and behavioral impairment are major sources of disability in primary tauopathies such as progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP) and corticobasal syndrome (CBS), yet evidence remains fragmented. Systematic searches identified studies reporting summary-level data for cognitive, behavioral, and clinical severity outcomes in PSP and CBS. Random-effects meta-analyses using restricted maximum likelihood (REML) were performed. Heterogeneity was assessed with Q and I2. Small-study effects were explored using funnel plots and Egger's regression. Cognitive screening measures, particularly the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE), Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA), and Addenbrooke's Cognitive Examination (ACE) were the most reported outcomes. REML pooled estimates suggested broadly comparable performance across groups, whereas within-study comparisons indicated more severe global cognitive impairment in PSP. These findings provide a quantitative synthesis of cognitive and behavioral outcomes in PSP and CBS and support a differential cognitive profile.

title: Ophthalmological and genetic findings associated with CRB1 dysfunction in autosomal recessive retinitis pigmentosa.
abstract: Retinitis pigmentosa (RP) is an inherited disease of the retina. It is characterized by progressive degeneration of the retinal photoreceptor cells. This pathology is due to mutations in CRB1 gene that is encoded by the crumbs homolog 1 (CRB1) protein. The aim of this study is to identify the mutations in Algerian patients with Retinitis Pigmentosa and to assess their structural, and functional implications as well as their correlation with clinico-pathology features. PATIENTS AND METHODS: This study was performed in collaboration with the ophthalmological department of Farhat Hached Hospital, Sousse, Tunisia. Whole-exome sequencing was performed on an Algerian female patient (IV.3) presenting RP. Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) followed by Direct Sanger sequencing were performed in all family's members (III3, III4, IV.3, IV4 and IV5,) to validate the mode of inheritance and confirm the disease segregation. Bioinformatics tools, including PolyPhen, were used to predict the pathogenicity through a scoring system, while SWISS-MODEL, PyMOL, InterProt and AlphaFold Server were performed for CRB1 structural modeling and to assess the impact of the mutations on its three-dimensional structure stability and flexibility. RESULTS: Based on the ophthalmological investigation, including fundus examination, Fluorescein Angiography (FA), and Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT), the two affected sisters (IV.3 and IV.4) exhibited a mottled fundus appearance with widespread areas of Retinal Pigment Epithelium (RPE) atrophy. FA demonstrated multiple hyperfluorescent areas consistent with window defects due to RPE loss, interspersed with relatively hypofluorescent regions corresponding to advanced chorioretinal atrophy. A relatively preserved central hyperfluorescent island was observed. OCT revealed marked degeneration of the outer retinal layers, with thinning of the photoreceptor layer, particularly in the peripheral retina. These findings initially suggested a choroideremia-like phenotype. Whole-exome sequencing identified a homozygous pathogenic variant in CRB1 gene (p.Glu710Val) in two affected sisters (IV.3 and IV4) by the autosomal recessive Retinitis Pigmentosa form, while no pathogenic variants were detected in CHM gene. The structural analysis revealed that the residue 710 is located in a domain Laminin G-like (LG) of the crumbs homolog 1 (CRB1) protein rather than in a calcium-binding EGF-like domain. The p.Glu710Val substitution abolishes a stabilizing hydrogen bond with Gln853, thereby disrupting the local interaction network within the Laminin G-like domain. The loss of this polar interaction may reduce local structural stability and alter the microenvironment of this domain. This is the first ophthalmological and molecular report of autosomal recessive Retinitis Pigmentosa in Algerian patients. Although ophthalmological investigation initially suggested a choroideremia-like phenotype, whole-exome sequencing identified a pathogenic CRB1variant, while only benign variants were detected in CHM gene. This case highlights the phenotypic overlap between inherited retinal dystrophies and underscores the importance of combining comprehensive ophthalmic assessment with molecular genetic testing for accurate diagnosis.

title: The critical role of cerebrospinal fluid-contacting neurons in spinal cord injury repair mediated by treadmill training.
abstract: Adult neural stem cells play a significant role in promoting motor function recovery after spinal cord injury (SCI) through rehabilitative exercise. However, it remains unclear whether cerebrospinal fluid-contacting neurons (CSF-cNs), which possess the potential to act as neural stem cells, are involved in treadmill training-facilitated SCI repair. This study aimed to investigate the role of CSF-cNs in this process. Treadmill training was performed on female C57BL/6 mice with SCI to assess the activation and proliferation of CSF-cNs with neural stem cell potential. The effects of treadmill training on axonal growth, myelin regeneration, tissue repair, and motor function recovery were evaluated. To further validate the role of CSF-cNs in exercise-induced spinal cord repair, Pkd2l1-/- mice exhibiting CSF-cNs depletion underwent treadmill training after SCI, and the resulting changes in neural stem cell proliferation and spinal cord repair were assessed. Treadmill training activated the neural stem cell potential of CSF-cNs, promoted their proliferation, and was accompanied by enhanced axon growth, myelin regeneration, and motor function recovery. In contrast, a significant reduction in proliferating cells around the central canal of the spinal cord was observed in Pkd2l1-/- mice. Furthermore, deletion of Pkd2l1 significantly attenuated the beneficial effects of treadmill training on motor function recovery in SCI mice. CSF-cNs play a critical role in SCI recovery enhanced by treadmill training. These findings highlight the potential of CSF-cNs as a therapeutic target for the development of novel strategies to treat SCI.

title: Alcohol Cues Invigorate Aversion-Resistant Alcohol Drinking.
abstract: Alcohol use disorder is characterized by continued alcohol use despite negative consequences, also known as aversion-resistant drinking. Alcohol-related cues can invigorate motivation to seek and consume alcohol. It is currently unknown whether alcohol-related cues can invigorate drinking despite negative consequences. Long-Evans rats were trained in a discriminative stimulus (DS) task with cues predicting the availability of an alcohol reward. They were then tested in the task for aversion-resistant drinking by measuring consumption of alcohol adulterated with increasing concentrations of quinine. As a control for an environment free of explicit reward-related cues, rats were also tested for aversion-resistant drinking in the home cage. We found that rats displayed robust aversion-resistant drinking in the DS task. When we compared alcohol consumption in the task with home cage consumption, we found that rats were more aversion resistant in the task than in the home cage. We also found that individual differences in aversion-resistant drinking were correlated within behavioral context (i.e., home cage or DS task) but not between the home cage and the DS task. We found that aversion-resistant drinking is invigorated during cue-induced alcohol seeking relative to free drinking without explicit alcohol cues. Home cage quinine sensitivity is unrelated to quinine sensitivity in the presence of cues. This suggests that cues motivate drinking despite negative consequences in a way that is unique from aversion resistance driven by drinking history. Although many behavioral measures use cues and ultimately test aversion-resistant drinking, this is the first explicit test of cue-evoked aversion-resistant drinking.

title: Impact of vibegron on quality of life in men with overactive bladder receiving treatment for benign prostatic hyperplasia: patient-reported outcomes from the randomized placebo-controlled COURAGE trial.
journal: Health and quality of life outcomes
abstract: Men receiving pharmacologic treatment for benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) may experience reduced quality of life (QoL) owing to persistent overactive bladder (OAB) symptoms. Vibegron, a β3-adrenergic receptor agonist, was approved for OAB symptoms based on the COURAGE trial. We present exploratory patient-reported outcomes from COURAGE. Eligible men were ≥ 45 years old with OAB symptoms receiving BPH treatment (α-blocker ± 5α-reductase inhibitor). Patients were randomly assigned 1:1 to receive vibegron 75 mg or placebo for 24 weeks. Patients completed the OAB questionnaire (OAB-q) and Patient Global Impression (PGI) scales at baseline and weeks 12 and 24. Changes from baseline in OAB-q subscores and PGI scales were assessed. An anchor-based approach was used to determine the distribution of change from baseline in COURAGE trial endpoints (micturitions, urgency, nocturia, and urge urinary incontinence [UUI] episodes) by category of change on the PGI change (PGI-C) scale. Of 1105 patients (vibegron, n = 551; placebo, n = 554); 1080 (vibegron, n = 538; placebo, n = 542) had evaluable data and were included in the analysis. Baseline mean OAB-q and PGI scores were similar between treatment groups. Patients receiving vibegron had statistically significantly greater improvements vs. placebo from baseline to week 12 (P < 0.05) for all OAB-q subscale scores and improvements remained statistically significant at week 24 (P < 0.05), except for social interaction. Patients receiving vibegron had improvements from baseline on all PGI endpoints at weeks 12 and 24. A higher percentage of patients receiving vibegron (81.9%) reported improvement on the PGI-C vs. placebo (69.3%). Patients receiving vibegron who reported moderately or much better on the PGI-C scale demonstrated improvement in mean change from baseline to week 12 in micturitions, urgency, nocturia, and UUI. Men with OAB symptoms receiving pharmacologic BPH treatment demonstrated statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in QoL with vibegron vs. placebo, consistent with improvements in OAB symptoms. Clinicaltrials.gov NCT03902080 Registered 04-01-2019.

title: Effectiveness of vaginal versus oral progesterone therapy in patients with endometrial hyperplasia: a randomized clinical trial.
abstract: Progesterone therapy is the main drug for the treatment of endometrial hyperplasia as a precursor of endometrial cancer. Considering the side effects of systemic progesterone use, we decided to compare the effectiveness and side effects of vaginal use versus oral use. This parallel group randomized clinical trial was conducted among 80 women with EH, without atypia, and abnormal uterine bleeding (AUB). Participants were allocated to two groups. Participants in group I received MPA, 2 tablets (5 mg) orally for 14 days per month for 3 months. Participants in group II obtained a 100 mg soft gelatin Progesterone capsule for vaginal use at the same time. 3-4 weeks after the completion of the treatment, the patient's endometrial thicknesses were measured, and endometrial samples were obtained. Finally, 39 and 36 participants were evaluated from groups I and II. The mean endometrial thickness significantly decreased after the intervention compared to before in each group (All p < 0.05), but no statistically significant difference was seen (P = 0.37) between groups. The clinical and histologic effects of vaginal MP are the same as MPA, after three cycles of treatment of EH without atypia. IRCT20140820018866N8. Registered 10/11/2019 Prospectively registered, https//www.irct.ir/trial/41,581.

title: Best1 shapes the depth and stability of NREM sleep.
abstract: Sleep architecture is orchestrated by neuronal circuits, yet the contribution of astrocytes-particularly to the depth and continuity of sleep-remains incompletely understood. Mammalian sleep is composed of rapid eye movement (REM) and non-REM (NREM) stages, with NREM further subdivided into light and deep phases. While neuronal and neurotransmitter-based mechanisms of sleep regulation have been extensively characterized, the role of astrocytic signaling in deep NREM sleep has received relatively little attention. Bestrophin-1 (Best1) is a calcium-activated anion channel highly enriched in astrocytes, known to mediate non-vesicular release of gliotransmitters such as glutamate, D-serine, and GABA, and to influence neuronal excitability. Here, we identify Best1 as a critical regulator of deep NREM sleep. Immunohistochemistry revealed robust Best1 expression in astrocytes across sleep-regulating brain regions. EEG/EMG polysomnography in Best1 knockout (Best1-KO) mice demonstrated a selective disruption of deep NREM sleep, despite preserved total sleep time and overall NREM duration. Best1-KO mice exhibited shorter deep NREM bouts, attenuated delta-band (0.5-4 Hz) EEG power, and altered vigilance-state transitions, with reduced entry into and maintenance of deep NREM. Sleep trajectories were biased toward Wake → light NREM → REM transitions, frequently bypassing deep sleep stages. Spectral decomposition further confirmed diminished delta oscillations during NREM episodes. These findings establish Best1 as a substage-specific molecular gatekeeper of deep NREM sleep. By uncovering a glial mechanism that shapes sleep sub-architecture, this work highlights astrocytic ion signaling as a promising therapeutic target for disorders marked by fragmented or insufficient deep sleep, including those associated with aging and neurodegenerative disease.

title: Long‑term disease control in generalized myasthenia gravis: a systematic literature review.
abstract: Generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG) is an autoimmune disease, causing impaired muscle contraction and weakness with a debilitating impact on quality of life. Despite a range of established treatment options, long-term outcomes in people with gMG remain poorly understood. A systematic literature review (SLR) was conducted to identify evidence for long-term (> 1 year) disease control and remission in adults with gMG from observational studies published from 2000 onwards. This analysis focused on a subset of publications reporting data for ≥ 1 gMG disease states defined as remission, minimal manifestations (MMs), or change in status. In total, 67 publications from the SLR reported data for ≥ 1 disease states. There was heterogeneity across included studies in terms of disease characteristics, reported treatments, outcomes definitions, and follow-up approaches, which were reflected in outcome reporting variability. No clear trends based on changed disease state over time were observed, however the proportion of patients achieving key clinical goals was generally low. Notably, complete stable remission (CSR), pharmacological remission (PR), and uncategorized remission achievement rates did not exceed 10, 30, and 50%, respectively, at any follow-up timepoint in most studies. Similarly, the proportion of patients achieving MM status, as measured by MM-0, MM-1, and MM-2, remained below 5, 20, and 20%, respectively, across most studies. These results suggest that at least 50% of gMG patients experience persistent symptoms over many years of follow-up. The lack of any trends in improving disease status over time suggests that patients are unable to optimally manage their disease with current treatment options. The protocol for this systematic review has been registered in PROSPERO (CRD420250641579).

title: Clinical and treatment profiles of myasthenic crisis patients in a tertiary hospital in the Philippines: a single-center retrospective study.
abstract: Myasthenic crisis is a life-threatening complication of myasthenia gravis. Data on its clinical profile and outcomes in resource-limited settings are limited. A retrospective review of pediatric and adult myasthenic crisis patients admitted at Philippine General Hospital from 2015 to 2024 was conducted. Sociodemographic, clinical, treatment, and outcome data were extracted from inpatient charts. Descriptive statistics and Pearson's chi-square, Fisher's exact, Wilcoxon rank-sum, and Kruskal-Wallis tests were used to analyze associations between clinical characteristics and outcomes. Eighty-two patients were included, mostly female (n = 49, 59.8%) with peak onset in the third decade. Infection was the leading precipitant of crisis, while hypertension, diabetes, and tuberculosis were common comorbidities. Nearly all required ventilation (96.3%, median nine days). Mortality was 13.4% (n = 11), mainly due to sepsis and respiratory failure. Younger age (< 30 years, p = 0.021) was linked to improved survival, whereas absence of intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) or therapeutic plasma exchange (TPE) was associated with higher mortality (p = 0.012). This study provided one of the largest descriptions of myasthenic crisis in the Philippines, demonstrating that infection remains the predominant inciting factor and timely rescue immunotherapy is associated with improved survival. These findings support strengthening access to specialized neuromuscular care and crisis-directed therapies in resource-constrained settings.

title: MigrAInet: a European multidisciplinary initiative to advance precision migraine medicine through artificial intelligence.
journal: The journal of headache and pain

title: The glioblastoma spider web: multidimensional crosstalk within the tumor microenvironment and therapeutic implications.
abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) exhibits profound therapeutic resistance and aggressive recurrence, driven not solely by tumor-intrinsic mutations, but by a highly integrated, dynamically evolving tumor microenvironment (TME). In this review, we propose the "GBM Spider Web" model to conceptualize the multidimensional and spatiotemporal crosstalk among immune cells, neurons, glial cells, and the extracellular matrix. We systematically deconstruct this ecosystem, highlighting emerging biological paradigms such as neuron-glioma synaptic communication, astrocyte-mediated mitochondrial transfer, and mechanometabolic reprogramming orchestrated by severe hypoxia and lactate accumulation. Crucially, we elucidate how these diverse microenvironmental stressors converge upon a central signaling nexus, primarily integrating the nuclear factor-κB (NF-κB), Wnt/β-catenin, and phosphoinositide 3-kinase/protein kinase B/mammalian target of rapamycin (PI3K/Akt/mTOR) pathways to drive adaptive evolution, immune evasion, and macroscopic functional syncytium. Furthermore, we comprehensively evaluate next-generation therapeutic strategies designed to disrupt this robust network, ranging from advanced immunotherapies and nanotechnology-based interventions to adaptive physical therapies and the novel targeting of meningeal lymphatic drainage. By shifting the paradigm from isolated tumor-centric pathways to a systemic, network-based perspective, this review provides a strategic framework for overcoming adaptive resistance and guiding the rational design of combinatorial therapies for GBM.

title: Bioequivalence of two formulations of amitriptyline hydrochloride tablets in healthy Chinese subjects under fasting and fed conditions.
abstract: The study evaluated the bioequivalence and tolerability of a generic amitriptyline hydrochloride tablet compared to the reference product in healthy Chinese subjects under both fasting and postprandial conditions to support its marketing authorization. A single-center, open-label, randomized, single-dose, two-period, two-sequence crossover study was conducted. Eligible subjects took a single 25 mg dose of the generic or reference product per cycle in random order. Plasma drug concentrations were detected by LC-MS/MS and the bioequivalence of the two formulations was assessed through key pharmacokinetic parameters (Cmax, AUC0-t, and AUC0-∞) of amitriptyline. Adverse events were continuously monitored throughout the trial. The 90% confidence intervals (CIs) for the geometric mean ratios (GMRs) of Cmax, AUC0-t, and AUC0-∞ between the two products fell within the 80-125% range under both fasting and postprandial conditions. Our study indicated that food intake increases systemic exposure to amitriptyline without affecting Tmax. Both formulations were well tolerated, with predominantly mild adverse events and no severe or fatal events. The generic amitriptyline hydrochloride tablets by Changzhou Siyao Pharmaceuticals Co., Ltd. were bioequivalent to the reference formulation by Sandoz Inc. with comparable tolerability. This study was registered at www.chinadrugtrials.org.cn under the registration number CTR20212242 (November 2, 2021).

title: The clinical, radiological, and genetic features of Pantothenate Kinase-Associated Neurodegeneration and Mitochondrial membrane Protein-Associated Neurodegeneration in Neurodegeneration with Brain Iron Accumulation: a case series.
abstract: Neurodegeneration with brain iron accumulation (NBIA) represents a group of rare, genetically heterogeneous neurodegenerative disorders characterized by excessive iron deposition in the basal ganglia, especially globus pallidus and substantia nigra. Among its subtypes, pantothenate kinase-associated neurodegeneration (PKAN) and mitochondrial membrane protein-associated neurodegeneration (MPAN) are among the most common NBIA subtypes. Reporting these cases is significant due to the rarity of NBIA, the diversity of its genetic etiologies, and the characteristic imaging patterns that aid early diagnosis. This series highlights the clinical and molecular spectrums of NBIA in an Indian cohort, emphasizing the diagnostic importance of integrating neuroimaging and genetic testing. Four children diagnosed with NBIA at a tertiary care hospital in South India were evaluated. Two unrelated children, a 4-year-old girl and a 6-year-old girl, from India, presented with early-onset dystonia, global developmental delay, and progressive motor disability. Brain MRI revealed the classic "eye-of-the-tiger" sign in the globus pallidus, and genetic testing identified pathogenic variants in the PANK2 gene, confirming PKAN. The remaining two children were a 16-year-old boy and a 16-year-old girl, first cousins from a consanguineous Muslim family in South India, developed gait disturbances and dysarthria in mid-childhood. MRI showed hyperintense streaking of the globus pallidus, and molecular analysis detected a likely pathogenic variant in the C19orf12 gene, confirming MPAN. All four children exhibited progressive motor decline, with supportive management focusing on physiotherapy, symptomatic control, and genetic counseling. This case series underscores the clinical and genetic heterogeneity of NBIA and the diagnostic value of characteristic MRI findings coupled with targeted genetic testing. Recognition of specific imaging patterns, such as the "eye-of-the-tiger" sign and hyperintense streaking of the globus pallidus, can guide clinicians toward accurate molecular diagnosis. Reporting such cases from diverse populations expands the understanding of NBIA's phenotypic spectrum and reinforces the need for multidisciplinary evaluation, early diagnosis, and family-based genetic counseling to optimize patient care and inform future therapeutic strategies.

title: Implementation science-guided rollout of a standalone radiology clinical decision support system in a tertiary emergency department: findings from a pragmatic controlled before-after study.
journal: BMC medical informatics and decision making
abstract: Radiological clinical decision support systems (CDSS) promote value-based healthcare and guide appropriate imaging; however, acceptance and uptake remain inconsistent. Suboptimal implementation can limit the effectiveness of CDSS, widening the research-practice gap. This study examined whether applying implementation science principles for standalone CDSS implementation influenced imaging appropriateness in the emergency department (ED). A pragmatic controlled before-and-after study was conducted. A purposive sample of junior ED physicians was recruited from the largest acute tertiary hospital in Singapore. Implementation science principles from a process model were incorporated in the implementation of the standalone CDSS. Appropriateness rates of X-ray cervical and lumbar spine were examined before and after "Do nothing" and availability of CDSS, respectively with reference to institutional imaging referral guidelines. Radiologically significant positive rates of imaging performed were also explored. Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, Mann-Whitney U tests and multilevel logistic regression models were performed. A total of 17 and 23 ED physicians participated in the control and intervention groups, respectively, yielding 593 and 755 imaging procedures for each group. Among physicians in the intervention group, CDSS adoption was 47.8% (n = 11/23). There were no statistically significant within-group and between-group changes in appropriateness rates. Patient age was strongly associated with appropriateness rate with each additional year of age increasing the appropriateness rate by 8% (OR = 1.08, 95% CI: 1.07-1.09, p < 0.001). Multilevel logistic regression revealed a strong association between appropriateness of imaging and positive radiological findings. Patients with appropriate imaging had higher odds of positive findings compared to inappropriate imaging patients (OR = 21.55, 95% CI: 2.88-161.3, p < 0.05), although the estimate was imprecise due to sparse data. Availability of CDSS in the ED did not significantly improve appropriateness rates of cervical and lumbar spine X-rays, suggesting limited practice change from implementing standalone CDSS. There were underlying issues, weaknesses, and gaps in the implementation strategies that constrained the potential of CDSS and warranted attention to optimise its effect on appropriate imaging. Not applicable.

title: Longitudinal exploration of auditory sensory-perceptual processing in CLN3 disease (Juvenile Neuronal Ceroid Lipofuscinosis (Batten disease)): A high-density auditory evoked potential (AEP) study.
abstract: There is currently limited information about sensory and perceptual abilities across the progression of CLN3 disease (Juvenile Neuronal Ceroid Lipofuscinosis; Batten disease), a recessively inherited lysosomal storage disorder and a leading cause of childhood neurodegeneration. Clinical symptoms include vision loss, motor impairments, and cognitive challenges, making it difficult to accurately assess neurocognitive and perceptual abilities. Thus, there is a critical need to identify objective biomarkers that can be used to inform disease progression and track treatment response in this population. This exploratory case series investigates longitudinal changes in auditory sensory perceptual processing over several years in a small sample of individuals with genetically confirmed CLN3 disease (N = 4; 3 male) compared to a cross-sectional sample of 60 neurotypical (NT) controls using high-density electroencephalography (EEG). We utilized a duration mismatch negativity (MMN) paradigm, identical to what has been used in our previous cross-sectional study. We examined the auditory evoked potentials (AEPs) of the standard tones across three different stimulus onset asynchrony conditions and examined the N1 and P2 components of the AEP. Early evidence shows differences in the amplitudes of the N1 and P2 components in individuals with CLN3 disease relative to NT controls. These amplitude differences were most notable in CLN3 disease when participants were presented with standard tones that had the slowest presentation rate. Specifically, N1 and P2 amplitudes were more negative than NT controls in childhood and adolescence and as CLN3 disease participants aged, the amplitude of the AEPs was more positive than controls. Further, a more positive N1 amplitude during the longest stimulus presentation condition was associated with both reduced verbal intelligence and working memory abilities in CLN3 disease participants. Our preliminary case-series findings parallel recently published work in a mouse model of CLN3 disease that showed both sex- and age-dependent disruptions in central auditory processing. Taken together, we demonstrate the utility of auditory EEG measures as a sensitive, objective and translational measure in CLN3 disease that may serve as a potential outcome measure useful in tracking disease progression. Continued work is needed in humans focused on sex-based differences and longitudinal changes of auditory processing in CLN3 disease.

title: Early motor development in ADHD: monogenic and polygenic trajectories using NF1 as a model.
abstract: ADHD is often accompanied by motor difficulties in childhood, yet little is known about how these traits emerge in early life or the genetic pathways that contribute to their development. Studying infants with an elevated familial likelihood of ADHD (EL-ADHD) alongside those with a monogenic condition associated with ADHD, such as Neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1), provides a unique opportunity to compare polygenic and monogenic influences on early motor development and its relationship to later ADHD traits. Accordingly, this study examined motor profiles in EL-ADHD, NF1, and typically developing (TD) infants, and investigated how early motor behaviour relates to emerging ADHD characteristics. The motor behaviour of infants with EL-ADHD, NF1, and TD were assessed at 10 and 14 months using a multimodal approach that included standardized motor assessments, parent reports of activity levels, behavioural coding of movements during free play, and accelerometery. Early ADHD traits were subsequently evaluated at follow-up visits at ages 2 and 3 years using the Child Behaviour Checklist (CBCL). Across infancy, EL-ADHD infants exhibited higher gross motor scores on standardised assessments compared to TD and NF1 infants, although they did not differ from either group in their fine motor scores. In contrast, NF1 infants showed both lower gross and fine motor scores relative to TD and EL-ADHD peers. During free play, EL-ADHD infants displayed more mature motor behaviours and marginially higher mean acceleration levels compared to TD and NF1 infants, whereas only minimal free play differences were observed between TD and NF1. Additionally, group-specific relationships emerged between motor behaviour and later ADHD traits. In the EL-ADHD group only, 14-month gross motor skills showed a trend-level positive association with ADHD traits at 36 months, and 14-month parent-reported activity levels significantly predicted ADHD traits at both 24 and 36 months. This study is the first to examine the relationship between motor development and ADHD traits in both polygenic and monogenic contexts. Our findings show that motor difficulties emerge early in infants with NF1, whereas such difficulties are not evident in those at elevated likelihood of ADHD in the general population. Moreover, early motor behaviour predicts later ADHD traits in ways that are specific to both developmental context and population. These results suggest that ADHD phenotypes can arise through distinct neurodevelopmental trajectories across different atypically developing populations.

title: Cellular Senescence at the Blood-Brain Barrier: a Potential Driver of Vulnerability and Poor Recovery in Ischaemic Stroke.
abstract: Advancing age is the strongest non-modifiable risk factor for ischaemic stroke and a major determinant of injury severity and functional recovery, yet the biological mechanisms through which ageing amplifies cerebrovascular vulnerability remain incompletely understood. Emerging evidence indicates that ageing-associated vascular dysfunction and cellular senescence converge at the level of the blood-brain barrier (BBB), transforming it from a protective interface into a critical mediator of ischaemic injury. In this review, we synthesise clinical, experimental, and translational data demonstrating that BBB dysfunction develops early during ageing, exhibits regional and genetic vulnerability, and is closely linked to senescence of endothelial cells and pericytes within the neurovascular unit. Senescence-associated alterations in cellular metabolism, inflammatory signalling, fibrinolytic balance, and endothelial-pericyte crosstalk compromise barrier integrity, promote leukocyte infiltration, and lower the threshold for ischaemic damage. Importantly, cerebral ischaemia itself accelerates senescence programmes, establishing a self-reinforcing cycle in which vascular ageing and ischaemic injury potentiate one another and constrain post-stroke repair. We further highlight emerging preclinical evidence that targeting senescent cells or rejuvenating the ageing BBB restores barrier function, attenuates neuroinflammation, and improves neurological outcomes, particularly in aged models. Collectively, these findings position BBB senescence as a central and modifiable mechanism linking ageing to ischaemic stroke susceptibility and recovery, and identify senescence-directed strategies as a promising therapeutic avenue for the ageing stroke population.

title: Child Sexual Abuse, Sexual Function, and Sexual Distress in Couples Coping with Sexual Interest/Arousal Disorder: A Dyadic Longitudinal Study.
abstract: Sexual interest/arousal disorder (SIAD), characterized by low sexual desire and high sexual distress, is the most common sexual dysfunction among women. Although current theoretical models support interpersonal conceptualizations of sexual desire, distal interpersonal factors that may underlie the sexual well-being of couples coping with SIAD, such as child sexual abuse (CSA), have not been thoroughly documented. Yet, difficulties with sexual desire and arousal are among the most frequently reported sexual dysfunctions among CSA survivors. Using a one-year longitudinal design among couples with SIAD, this study examined the associations between both partners' CSA and their sexual function and distress. Individuals with SIAD (N = 263; Mage = 34.16) and their partners (N = 263; Mage = 35.71) completed validated questionnaires at baseline, 6 months, and 12 months. Dyadic latent growth curve analyses were conducted within a structural equation model. Results showed that greater CSA among individuals with SIAD was associated with their own higher initial levels of sexual distress. Moreover, higher levels of non-SIAD partners' CSA were unexpectedly associated with lower initial levels of sexual function difficulties for individuals with SIAD. However, non-SIAD partners' CSA predicted greater increases in sexual function difficulties over time for individuals with SIAD. No other significant associations were found. Findings highlight the role of CSA in the sexual function and distress of couples coping with SIAD and point towards the value of couple-based interventions that acknowledge both partners' histories and their impact on mutual sexual experiences.

title: Super-enhancer-dependent transcriptional and m⁶A-mediated post-transcriptional regulation cooperatively drive lncRNA H19 to promote ESCC progression.
abstract: Epigenetic dysregulation mediated by long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), super-enhancers (SEs), and m⁶A modification remains incompletely characterized in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). ChIP-qPCR, dual-luciferase reporter assays and CRISPRi were performed to investigate the transcriptional regulation mechanism of H19 by super-enhancer. The functions and downstream signal transduction mechanisms of the H19 in ESCC were explored by a series of in vitro and in vivo assays, including RNA stability, RIP-qPCR, and MeRIP-qPCR. Furthermore, single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and pseudotime trajectory analysis were used to analyze its correlation with ESCC patient survival. We identified H19, a super-enhancer-driven lncRNA, as a critical oncogenic factor in ESCC, with its overexpression significantly correlating with poor patient prognosis. Mechanistically, the master transcription factor KLF5 binds the super-enhancer region of H19 locus to drive its transcriptional activation. Post-transcriptionally, H19 interacts with the m⁶A methylation reader protein IGF2BP2, which stabilizes H19 in an m⁶A-dependent manner mediated by METTL3. The resulting H19/IGF2BP2 complex upregulates the oncogenic Tweety family member 3 (TTYH3) by enhancing mRNA stability. Functional assays revealed that the H19/IGF2BP2-TTYH3 axis facilitates ESCC malignant progression, while the IGF2BP2 inhibitor CWI1-2 suppresses tumorigenesis. ScRNA-seq combined with pseudotime trajectory analysis further established a significant positive correlation between METTL3/IGF2BP2/TTYH3 expression and malignant phenotypes in ESCC. The H19/IGF2BP2-TTYH3 axis drives ESCC progression, providing valuable prognostic biomarkers and promising therapeutic targets for ESCC treatment.

title: SIMPATHY Study: Specific Antibody Response to Typhim Vi Polysaccharide as a Surrogate Marker of Infectious Risk in Secondary Immunodeficiency Associated with B Cell Cancer.
abstract: Recurrent and severe infections represent a major cause of morbidity and mortality of secondary immunodeficiency (SID) associated with B-cell lymphoproliferative syndromes (B-CLPD). Nevertheless, immunological evaluation and prophylactic interventions are often delayed until infectious complications occur. Early vaccination is therefore relevant not only because it provides protection during the initial phases of B-CLPD, but also because it enables the identification of patients at higher risk of infection. In this context, assessment of antigen-specific humoral response has been proposed as a useful biomarker for identifying patients with greater clinical vulnerability. We conducted SIMPATHY (Secondary Immunodeficiency Multicentric study on the Antibody Production to Typhi vaccine), a multicentre, retrospective, observational study including 128 individuals with B-CLPD, classified according to the presence or absence of severe and/or recurrent infections, as well as healthy controls. Specific IgG antibody responses to Streptococcus pneumoniae (13-valent conjugate, Prevenar), Salmonella typhi (Typhim Vi), and tetanus toxoid vaccines were assessed at baseline and 4-weeks after vaccination.
